Notation of baystability

Source: R/common-notation.R
bys_notation.Rd

The symbols used in the help pages and vignettes of baystability, with their meaning and the argument or result component that holds them. The notation follows one rule throughout: scalars are upper-case letters in normal face (\(P\), \(R\)), indices lower-case italic (\(i, j\)), vectors lower-case bold (\(\mathbf{y}\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\)) and matrices upper-case bold (\(\mathbf{X}\), \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\)).

Usage

bys_notation(format = c("table", "path", "tex"))

Arguments

format

"table" (default: a data.table with columns symbol (LaTeX), text (plain text), kind (scalar, index, vector, matrix, set, function, operator), meaning and argument), "path" (the path of notation.csv) or "tex" (the path of Notations.tex, the notation appendix used in the articles).

Value

See format.

See also

Other baystability utilities: bys_reference(), bys_save(), bys_theme()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

bys_notation(
    format = c("table", "path", "tex")[1]
  )
